records.region: South Texas: Jim Hogg and Brooks County plains, Vargas Creek along the northern Starr/Hidalgo County setting, inland small-water country and the Kenedy County coast.
records.candidate_name_role: Bounded mapped component candidates only; no established representative identity for the entire selected route.
records.material_pending_reason: Complete western opening and eastward/southward dryland transfer into Vargas Creek. Selected eastward transfer beyond the mapped Vargas Creek small-lake end, across US281 and into the separate drainage/small-water setting. Selected Callo Padrones bypass, southern turn and long inland northeastward passage through small-water and dryland surroundings. Selected US77 crossing and complete cross-plain approach to Cayo Soledad. Selected marsh/land through-transfer from Cayo Soledad to the actual coastal lagoon endpoint.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected modeled line begins far west of the mapped Vargas Creek, crosses its middle corridor, extends east and southeast beyond the creek-end small lake, turns north through inland small-water country, crosses US77 and reaches Cayo Soledad before ending farther east at the tidal-lagoon edge. Nearby named waters are not substituted for selected connectors.
records.completion_scope: The bounded four-original source pass is finished. The river-group finding remains one material-pending record because the identified headward, inland and coastal through-links are unestablished. There is no completed representative identity, completed naming-scope hold or additional access-pending classification.
records.supported_name_scope: Vargas Creek identifies the mapped middle creek corridor. Cayo Soledad identifies the mapped coastal waterbody passage. Neither establishes a through-system name for the long intervening and headward selected dryland/small-water links.

component_scope_limits: Vargas Creek and Cayo Soledad are distinct bounded component names, not alternatives for one whole modeled river.

records.region: Eastern interior Victoria Island, Arctic Canada; lake-and-stream corridor north of Washburn Lake, followed east toward a north-turning coastal approach.
records.material_pending_reason: Original source coverage ends at the eastern Washburn Lake sheet edge, before the selected northward lower reach and actual terminal. The sole adjacent Denmark Bay map request lost terminal-status visibility after an authorization-context refusal and one identical retry returned an unknown process. No adjacent source pixels were read. Model continuity cannot replace this missing geographic correspondence.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected opening, western lake succession, long central lake, intervening eastern lake links and the lower eastward river corridor are present on the Washburn Lake land-resource map at ordinary corridor scale. The selected final northward reach and actual terminal lie beyond that map's eastern neatline. The adjacent Denmark Bay original was not confirmed acquired, so no receiving-bay identity or complete whole-system correspondence is asserted.
records.completion_scope: The usable original was read over the selected portion within its coverage, including the opening and the lake/channel joins before the eastern map edge. All48 selected constituent sublines were accounted for in the coverage assessment. The final cross-sheet continuation, northward lower reach and actual coastal terminal remain materially unsupported. This is one source-material-pending result, not completed representative identity or completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: No river or selected lake name was established from the original map inspected. Washburn Lake is the publication title and a different mapped lake, not a name for this selected northern corridor.

scope_limits: The map title Washburn Lake is not the name of the selected northern river/lake corridor.
Mapped neighboring lakes and bays do not establish the actual terminal or repair missing cross-sheet correspondence.
Historical map silence does not establish that the waters lack current local or official names.
The source's seasonal-water and interim-information cautions preclude claims of year-round flow or precise present-day channels.

records.region: Southern Patagonia, San Gregorio in Chile and southern Santa Cruz in Argentina, Ciaike/Chaike–Chico corridor to the Gallegos estuarine area.
records.candidate_name_role: Río Chico is supported for the receiving Argentine course and mouth. Chilean source labels have narrower reach scope; the representative whole-object identity remains pending because the selected border-aligned connector is unresolved.
records.material_pending_reason: The existing originals show the natural Ciaike/Chaike–Chico watercourse farther south near Laguna Timone and Estancia Brazo Norte. They place the selected middle fragment in the border-marker/land setting, but do not positively identify the entire selected connector as a particular non-river feature or establish a waterway, lake or managed transfer along it. The unresolved selected connector is a source-material gap, despite readable map coverage.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The western selected opening is an unnamed Chilean feeder, followed by the Ciaike/Chaike network and Río Chico receiving course. This is not the separate main Río Gallegos upstream course. Both originals show the natural river south of the selected border-aligned middle fragment. They do not establish the selected connector as a waterway or positively identify its full extent as a particular non-river feature. Nearby Timone, Pali Aike and Bismarck water bodies do not supply a demonstrated selected through-lake connection.
records.completion_scope: The bounded original-source inspection covers the western opening, each of the three stored fragments, their joins, the lower named course and actual Chico estuarine endpoint. This does not complete whole-selection identity: the border-aligned middle fragment and adjoining northward departure and southward return have no established through-connection or positively identified alternative feature. No further acquisition was made to turn absence of a mapped channel into a completed scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Mapped Chilean Ciaike/Chaike o Chico reaches, a source-labelled Pozuelos connecting reach, and the Argentine Río Chico receiving course; the initial feeder and border-aligned connector remain unnamed.

component_scope_limits: The initial MMA Quebrada has a blank name attribute; null does not mean no local or official name exists.
MMA segment-level Río de los Pozuelos and Río Chaike o Chico attributes are retained as source-specific reach evidence; they do not impose a single name on all parts.

Both originals show the natural river south of the selected border-aligned passage. They do not establish the selected through-waterway or positively identify its whole extent as a particular non-river feature; no lake, wetland or managed-transfer explanation is supplied.
Historical source cartography and an undated hydrography service do not establish current channel conditions, exact banks, discharge or tidal stage.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
